requirement:
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:

- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
  including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
  `habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
  partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
  selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
  active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.

Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.

A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.

If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace` has no review roots and no {impl} edges. Every clause I checked specifies observable behavior only.

- "atomically establishes the new coverage set" and "If the atomic replacement cannot be committed ... The previously committed coverage set and active configuration remain unchanged": this describes an outcome. After a failed commit, the old set and configuration are intact and no tests start. A SQL transaction, a write-then-rename, a single-file swap, or an in-memory swap followed by one persist would all give that outcome. None of them is mandated, so the mechanism is discretionary.
- The clauses on unfiltered and filtered invocations, pending entries without measurements, tests that never start staying unavailable, and empty selections describe which stored results exist after the replacement. They don't name a library, algorithm, type, field, signature, or delegation through a named interface. A different implementation could produce the same results and still satisfy the text.
- "After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected test starts" is an ordering of observable events. It doesn't prescribe a structure.

No clause prescribes how the implementation is built, so no implementation evidence is needed and no missing root exists. Test adequacy for the behaviors belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request any implementation source.

- **Unfiltered workspace clears the whole prior set, including removed tests.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[default_coverage_and_test_replace_removed_tests]` runs both `habeas coverage` with no arguments and the full `habeas test` flow. It asserts the prior run is gone and that only the current test remains. The final part of `package_binary_partition_and_ignored_selection_replace_only_their_actual_test_identities` also shows that `coverage` with no arguments replaces the whole set.
- **Filtered invocations clear only the selected identities and preserve the unselected ones.**
  - The integration test `package_binary_partition_and_ignored_selection_replace_only_their_actual_test_identities` covers package (`-p`), binary (`--lib`, `--test`), test filter (`-E`), `--partition` and `--run-ignored only`. It asserts that unselected metadata and measurements are unchanged and that the configuration is unchanged.
  - `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_replacement_preserves_unselected_results_and_shared_artifacts]` covers the store level, including same-named tests in different binaries and shared artifacts.
  - `real_parallel_processes_retries_child_profiles_and_filtered_reruns` also reruns filtered selections.
- **Every selected test gets a pending entry without measurements.** The store test asserts the replaced test is `pending` with `measurements.is_none()`. The fail-fast, interruption and startup-failure tests assert the same for every selected test.
- **Filtered versus unfiltered classification.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#mod[tests]/fn[explicit_filters_are_distinguished_from_workspace_run_settings]` checks that `--workspace`, `--all`, `--run-ignored all`, `--run-ignored=default`, retries, `-j`, profile, features and `--include-ignored` leave a run unfiltered. It also checks that `-p`, `--lib`, `--exclude`, `--run-ignored=only`, `--partition`, `-E`, a name filter, `--ignored` and `--skip` make it filtered.
  - The integration test sets a native `default-filter` and runs `--workspace --run-ignored all`. It asserts the whole set is replaced by only the default-filtered tests. It then asserts that default ignored handling still applies to a plain `coverage` run.
- **Selected tests that never start stay unavailable, with their previous result not restored.**
  - Fail-fast: `fail_fast_leaves_every_unstarted_selected_test_pending_without_old_measurements`.
  - Interruption: `interrupting_the_parent_preserves_started_attempt_metadata`.
  - Execution startup failure: `execution_startup_failure_leaves_prior_selected_results_pending_without_measurements`.
  - Each asserts the old run is gone, the unstarted tests are `pending` with no processes, and the saved check does not report complete results.
- **Empty selections.**
  - Filtered and empty: `real_parallel_processes_retries_child_profiles_and_filtered_reruns` asserts that runs and attempts are unchanged, with and without `--no-tests pass`. The store test `incompatible_builds_reset_every_test_but_empty_focused_runs_do_not` asserts the results and configuration are preserved.
  - Unfiltered and empty: the store test `focused_replacement_preserves_unselected_results_and_shared_artifacts` replaces with an empty unfiltered selection and asserts that no tests remain.
- **Commit failure.**
  - Store level: `failed_atomic_replacement_preserves_results_configuration_and_invocation` uses a failing trigger. It asserts an error, and unchanged configuration, latest invocation and measurements.
  - End to end: `a_failed_replacement_commit_reports_the_error_without_launching_execution` asserts the error is reported on stderr and that a sentinel `cargo` wrapper never sees `nextest run` execution start. It also asserts the prior runs and profiles are unchanged.
- **Selection discovery failure.** `selection_discovery_failure_preserves_existing_results_and_configuration` asserts the failure is reported and that existing runs, measurements and configuration are unchanged.

`collector_ownership_is_released_when_the_owner_exits` is marked for this requirement but is only tangential. The obligations above are covered without it.
